doc.citation: García Muro, V. J., Rubinstein, C. V. & Steemans, P. 2014. Upper Silurian miospores from the Precordillera Basin, Argentina: biostratigraphic, palaeonvironmental and palaeogeographic implications. Geological Magazine 151(3), 472–490.
doc.comment: Eighteen newly studied samples: 14 productive and four barren. Authors favour Ludlow but cannot exclude Pridoli; some spores suggest younger ages, and previously published conodont age assignments conflict. Possible reworking of Hispanaediscus wenlockensis is discussed. Figure 4 dotted, supposed ranges are excluded. Chart abbreviations and spelling are retained; bibliographic symbols are omitted. Caption/prose records absent from the chart are included. Qualified caption identifications differing from unqualified chart records are retained separately. The stated 43-species list excludes Retusotriletes sp. illustrated in Figure 7o. Literature comparisons are not treated as additional newly studied assemblages.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 1 (60667); 0.2 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore correlation and marine phytoplankton. Chelinospora verrucata places this sample no older than the base of the LP Biozone, interpreted as latest Homerian or earliest Gorstian; acritarchs indicate an age not older than Ludlow.
items.notes: Marine acritarchs and chlorophytes dominate the formation's palynological assemblages. Chelinohilates lornensis was previously known from the lowest Lochkovian of Scotland, but the authors retain a Late Silurian interpretation here.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 2 (60704); 0.4 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospores and marine phytoplankton. Stellatispora inframurinata var. inframurinata indicates the youngest LP subzone; Coronaspora cromatica and Concentricosisporites agradabilis are interpreted as pointing to latest Ludfordian.
items.notes: Concentricosisporites agradabilis is explicitly reported from this sample in section 6 although its Figure 4 range starts at sample 3. The chart identifies Archaeozonotriletes chulus with a dashed, cf. segment.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 3 (60659); 1.6 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore correlation and marine phytoplankton; acritarchs support Ludlow. Breconisporites sp. B occurs below its previously reported Lochkovian occurrence.
items.notes: Hispanaediscus wenlockensis could be reworked because its previously known occurrence was restricted to the type Wenlock area of England. Other species in samples 2 and 3 are considered stratigraphically in situ. The verrucate tetrad has no reported genus.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 4 (62521); 2.4 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospores and marine phytoplankton. Chelinospora cf. C. hemiesferica is correlated with the H Zone, interpreted as late Ludfordian and/or early Pridoli; Synorisporites verrucatus is not considered restricted to Pridoli.
items.notes: Contains Hispanaediscus wenlockensis, discussed as potentially reworked. Ambitisporites is represented by a dashed cf. segment in Figure 4; its printed taxon label lacks an explicit cf. The spelling hemisferica follows Figure 4, whereas the systematic heading uses hemiesferica.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 5 (62523); 3.8 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore correlation and marine phytoplankton; acritarchs support Ludlow. No first appearances of biostratigraphically relevant taxa are reported for this sample.
items.notes: Only continuous or dashed Figure 4 segments are extracted; dotted supposed ranges are excluded.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 6 (60662); 4.2 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore correlation and marine phytoplankton; acritarchs support Ludlow. No first appearances of biostratigraphically relevant taxa are reported for this sample.
items.notes: Coronaspora cromatica is shown by a dashed cf. segment. The abbreviated Dyadospora morphon label follows Figure 4; the systematic list spells the genus Dyadospora, whereas Figure 5c spells it Dyadaspora.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 7 (60736); 8 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Synorisporites tripapillatus, characteristic of the TS Zone, supports an age very close to the Ludlow–Pridoli boundary; marine phytoplankton support Ludlow.
items.notes: Figure 4 records unqualified E. rotatus, whereas Figure 8e identifies the specimen from slide 60736 as Emphanisporites cf. E. rotatus. Both reported identifications are retained.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 8 (60677); 20 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore correlation with Upper Silurian biozones and marine phytoplankton supporting Ludlow.
items.notes: Figure 4 records unqualified C. agradabilis, whereas Figure 6k identifies the specimen from slide 60677 as cf. Concentricosisporites agradabilis. Both reported identifications are retained.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 9 (60664); 23 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospores and marine phytoplankton. Brochotriletes foveolatus is compared with lower Pridoli Brazil; Leonispora argovejae suggests Lochkovian, but the authors consider spore definition of the Silurian–Devonian boundary uncertain and retain Late Silurian.
items.notes: Several taxa previously associated with Devonian assemblages occur here. The authors interpret these as compatible with a Late Silurian age rather than demonstrating Devonian deposition.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 10 (60673); 26 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore correlation with Upper Silurian biozones and marine phytoplankton supporting Ludlow.
items.notes: Contains Hispanaediscus wenlockensis, discussed as potentially reworked. Figure 4 records unqualified E. rotatus; Figure 8d identifies the specimen from slide 60673 as Emphanisporites cf. E. rotatus. Both reported identifications are retained.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 11 (61020); 227 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore and marine phytoplankton biostratigraphy. Marine palynomorphs support Ludlow, but the authors cannot exclude Pridoli for the youngest samples.
items.notes: Upper-section marine phytoplankton diversity decreases significantly; Pridoli index phytoplankton were not recorded. The upper third of the formation includes subaerial exposure at the tops of regressive cycles.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 12 (60986); 228 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore and marine phytoplankton biostratigraphy. Marine palynomorphs support Ludlow, but Pridoli cannot be excluded for the youngest samples.
items.notes: Contains Hispanaediscus wenlockensis, discussed as potentially reworked. Upper-section diversity and preservation decline towards the formation top.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 13 (60984); 229 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospores and marine phytoplankton. Amicosporites streelii indicates Lochkovian by its established record, but similar Upper Silurian Saudi Arabian specimens and the phytoplankton evidence lead the authors to retain Late Silurian.
items.notes: Emphanisporites protophanus is illustrated from slide 60984 in Figure 8b although Figure 4 does not record it at sample 13. Retusotriletes sp. is illustrated in Figure 7o but absent from the chart and systematic list. Figure 6l prints slide 600984 for cf. Concentricosisporites sagittarius; its sample assignment is independently supported by Figure 4. Chelinospora obscura is a dashed cf. record here.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 14 (60982); 230 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore and marine phytoplankton biostratigraphy. Acritarchs support Ludlow, while Pridoli cannot be excluded for the youngest samples.
items.notes: Highest productive sample; the four overlying samples are barren. Although Sphaerasaccus glabellus has older published occurrences, the authors do not explicitly interpret it as reworked here.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 15 (60980); one of the four samples closest to the upper boundary
items.age_basis_detail: Position in the studied uppermost Los Espejos Formation; no sample-specific palynological age is available because the sample is barren.
items.notes: Spores were sought but not recovered. Figure 2 identifies this as a barren sample; section 4 states that all four samples closest to the upper boundary were barren. Palynomorph disappearance is discussed in relation to regressive shelf–shoreface facies and subaerial exposure.
